summary: Completed backend API regression and desktop/mobile UI smoke testing. Auth, protected access, dashboard, listings, searches, navigation, and responsive sidebar passed. Order status update failed because newly created orders return Mongo _id as id instead of the PB-* order id expected by the PATCH endpoint.

critical.issue: POST /api/orders returns id as the Mongo ObjectId (clean() overwrites the explicit PB-* id), but PATCH looks up the explicit PB-* id. The documented create -> status workflow therefore returns 404 Order not found.

ui_bugs.issue: Add customer navigates to Orders and opens no creation form/modal.

action_items: Fix order response identifier handling so POST /api/orders returns the PB-* order id and PATCH status can find it; alternatively make PATCH consistently accept the returned identifier.
Implement the customer/product/order creation flows behind the corresponding Add buttons instead of routing all Add actions to Orders.
Add brute-force login lockout after five failures and make seed_admin update an existing admin password when the configured password changes.
critical_code_review_comments: clean() unconditionally replaces an existing domain id with Mongo _id; this is the root cause of the order lifecycle failure.
Repeated status-* data-testid values are rendered for every badge, so they are not unique selectors on list pages; include the record id or use class-only status styling.
seed_data_creation: Created one TEST_-prefixed customer, product, and order during the regression test; no cleanup endpoint exists, so these remain as demo records.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Auth cookie login/me/logout, unauthenticated protection, dashboard, all sidebar destinations, customer/product/order searches, mobile sidebar, and no horizontal overflow passed. Re-run create-order -> PATCH status first after fixing identifier handling; then verify Add customer/product flows and unique test IDs.
rca of the issue: create_order stores both an explicit human id (PB-year-sequence) and Mongo _id. clean() sees _id and assigns doc['id'] = str(doc.pop('_id')), overwriting the explicit id in the response only. The database still stores the PB-* id, and update_status queries that field, so it cannot find the identifier returned to the client and responds 404.
